title: Bumpless transfer
equipment: Variable-speed booster pump with external valve authority
physicalPurpose: Keep the pressure controller aligned while another station owns the valve so later authority changes do not introduce avoidable output steps.
principalTechnique: Bumpless transfer through external applied-output tracking
objective: Transfer valve authority between an external station, Auto, and Manual without an avoidable command step and identify boundaries where exact bumpless transfer is infeasible.

simplifications: SP and PV are held unchanged for the exact transition update so authority-state alignment is isolated from feedback response.
Actuator limits are nonbinding in the teaching move, so the accepted external command is copied through an applied-position proxy; physical use requires fresh independent valve feedback.
The inactive-without-tracking state is a simulation-only failure diagnostic that applies external output without invoking the controller.
The lesson does not qualify physical actuator feedback freshness, communications delay, or selector topology.

baseline.limitation: The inactive controller remains at 40 percent while external authority moves the valve to 60 percent, creating a 20 percentage-point step when Auto takes authority.

change.decision: Feed independently observed applied output to Track throughout external authority, then change only authority to Auto.

disturbances: Tracked and untracked external 40-to-60 percent changes

acceptance.window: first Auto update after 60 percent Track
first Auto update after inactive 60 percent external output
first Manual update from 40 to 10 percent
first Manual update after adopting 40 percent

abortPredicates: Pressure, tracking, external, manual, or controller value is nonfinite
Pressure or valve command leaves its hard limit
Tracking input is stale, invalid, or not independently tied to applied output
safety.restorationMode: Station Disabled with 30 percent safe recirculation
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not exercise authority transfer on a physical pump without reviewed ownership, fresh applied-output feedback, actuator protection, rollback, and explicit approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Align an inactive PI controller with actual applied output and execute bounded Manual, Track, and Auto authority transfers.

learning.context: An external station may own the booster-pump valve while the pressure controller remains available to take authority later.
learning.reason: Lesson 27 made startup state truthful, but that state becomes stale if another authority moves the valve while the controller receives no updates.
theory: Bumpless transfer means the first requested output from the new authority matches the last physically applied output within tolerance. It does not promise zero future feedback action.
With integral action, Track copies external applied output into retained nominal controller state before the incremental update. An inactive untracked controller retains stale output.
The external manual station must adopt current applied output before taking Manual authority. The PID cannot repair an unrelated manual command after ownership changes.
Exact alignment is not guaranteed for P or PD positional control, stale tracking, infeasible outputs, binding limits, or unaccounted signal changes.
learning.workedPrediction: From 40 percent and 6 bar, tracking an external move to 60 percent predicts a 60 percent first Auto request and zero step. Without tracking, retained output stays 40 percent and the transition step is 20 percentage points. An unrelated 10 percent manual value produces a 30-point step from 40 percent Auto; adopting 40 predicts zero.
practicalPreparation: Verify authority owner, SP, PV, external applied output, tracking input and quality, requested/applied output, limits, transition timestamp, safe state, and simulation label.
Restore the Lesson 27 state at 6 bar and 40 percent; keep SP, PV, gains, timing, limits, plant, and seed equal across tracked and untracked runs.
learning.baseline: Move external applied output from 40 to 60 percent while deliberately leaving the controller inactive and untracked, then transfer to Auto and retain the first request.
learning.change: Restore, call Track with the independently observed applied output throughout the same external move, then change only authority to Auto. Repeat Auto-to-Manual with unrelated and pre-aligned manual values.
learning.comparison: Compare authority-transition output step and retained-state alignment error at the exact transition sample, then inspect subsequent pressure recovery separately.
learning.validation: Require tracked external-to-Auto and aligned Auto-to-Manual steps at or below 0.001 percentage points, expose at least 20 and 30 points in the corresponding unaligned cases, and reject invalid tracking or binding-limit comparisons.
learning.explanation: Tracking is information flow from the authority that controls the actuator to the controller that may control it next. Bumpless behavior therefore depends on both controller state and supervisor ownership.
learning.transfer: Use this contract before selectors, cascade handover, parallel schedules, or redundant controllers. Lesson 29 next proves that configuration and signal contributions are coherent inside each authoritative scan.
